Delta Council adopted the Official Community Plan 2024, “Housing Our Future” (Bylaw No. 8400), on July 8, 2024.

The OCP has a Scottsdale Exchange transit-oriented area. The City says it is Delta’s only provincially designated one, and that it crosses the municipal boundary from Surrey. The OCP sets a density of up to 4.0 floor space ratio and a minimum height of 12 storeys within 200 metres of the exchange. From 200 to 400 metres it sets 3.0 floor space ratio and 8 storeys. There are no residential parking requirements there, except accessible spaces.

The OCP names the Scott Road corridor as Delta’s only Frequent Transit Development Area, and lists the R6 Scott Road RapidBus corridor, the Scottsdale Exchange area and the 72 Avenue corridor among North Delta’s growth areas.

The North Delta Area Plan (revised March 2015) welcomes residential infill on smaller lots east of 112 Street between 72 and 90 Avenue. It also names mixed-use nodes at 80 Avenue and at Scottsdale, focused on 72 Avenue.

Delta changed its zoning in 2024 so that many single detached and duplex lots can have a secondary suite plus up to two detached suites (a garden suite or coach house). The rules differ by lot, so ask me or the City about an address.
From MLS® sales data (not an official source): the median lot size of detached houses sold from July 1 to October 8, 2026 was 6,600 square feet, across 20 sales with a recorded lot size.
